_comment: Weights and decay scales for ranking candidate panoramas at a location. Two of our imagery providers rank
candidates themselves — Mapillary and Panoramax both answer a location query with every picture in a box, and we
choose one. (GSV delegates selection to Google's StreetViewService, and Infra3d/Pannellum never search by
location.) The two rank on the same terms with the same weights so that they pick comparably; only the
resolution cap differs, because their camera fleets do.
Three consumers must agree on these numbers, which is why they live here rather than in any one of them:
MapillaryViewer.#scorePano and PanoramaxViewer.#scorePano pick the pano Explore displays, and score_pano
(scripts/check_streets_for_imagery.py) picks the pano whose capture date we record for a street. If those
disagreed, we would report a street as freshly imaged and then never show the imagery that said so (#4411).
The weights sum to 1, so a score is always in [0, 1]. models.utils.PanoScoring parses this into a typed shape,
so a typo fails loudly and this comment never reaches the browser.
Not here on purpose: the milliseconds-per-Julian-year divisor that turns a timestamp delta into an age. It is a
property of the calendar rather than a tuning knob, so each consumer names it as its own constant.
